answers:
Where do my notes live?
+

Your notes are stored locally on your device. Lattice is designed around keeping your research in your own hands.

Can I take my notes to another app?
+

Yes. Export your notes as Markdown files, a readable text format that works with many writing and note-taking apps.

How do I back up my research?
+

Export your notes as files and keep copies in a backup location you choose, such as an external drive. Lattice does not promise automatic cloud backup; you manage your exported backups.

What happens if I cancel?
+

Cancellation has no effect on files you have already exported. Those Markdown files remain yours to open, edit, and keep independently of Lattice.

designReview.method: Single qualitative review of actual captured desktop and mobile pixels. No numerical aesthetic score.

observations.observation: The desktop hero pairs a compact two-line serif proposition with a framed notebook illustration. The dark workflow action is prominent and the adjacent Peek inside link is clearly secondary.
observations.implication: Text, product preview and next actions are legible without the headline consuming the full opening composition.

observations.observation: Dark green serif headings, muted green italic emphasis, cream/sage surfaces, thin rules and small source/document motifs recur throughout. The Studio plan uses a dark inverse surface while preserving the same type and spacing language.
observations.implication: The page maintains a recognizable research-notebook identity across the hero, workflow, plans and FAQ.

observations.observation: The hero preview combines a notebook window, note contents and a source card extending outside the frame. The Connect panel links an observation card to a source; the workflow adds small project, source and Markdown illustrations.
observations.implication: The visuals teach the product’s source-and-note relationship instead of functioning only as decoration. Visible demonstration captions appropriately qualify the previews.

observations.observation: Main headings and descriptions are readable, but notebook toolbar labels, tiny preview metadata and captions are substantially smaller. In the mobile notebook preview those details become particularly fine.
observations.implication: The illustration communicates structure and atmosphere more readily than its individual small labels; it should not be treated as a readable product screenshot at every scale.

observations.observation: At the captured mobile width the two-line headline, explanation and both hero actions fit, and a sizeable portion of the notebook preview is visible below them. The header has an icon-only menu control.
observations.implication: The opening reveals the product illustration within the first screen while retaining a clear primary action. No obvious overlap or clipped primary text is visible; this does not certify the rest of the mobile page.

observations.observation: The pricing layout centers two plans with large yearly values and a strong visual emphasis on Studio through a dark card and light action button. The FAQ uses separate rows, a clearly expanded answer and a restrained final callout.
observations.implication: The information is readily scannable. The visual premium-plan emphasis is a presentation choice, not evidence of measured conversion or superior product value.

mobileLayoutObservation.note: The width values come from the capture receipt; they are not an aesthetic score.

limits: Only the supplied captured states were reviewed. Mobile coverage here is the initial viewport, not a complete mobile walkthrough.
Static viewport captures do not establish keyboard behavior, motion quality, all responsive states or measured color-contrast conformance.
Visual appearance does not reveal the generating agent’s planning, tool choices, verification method or experimental condition. Process evidence belongs in a separate analysis.
Some anchored captures begin partway through surrounding content; that is real viewport framing, not proof that the candidate clips that content.
The notebook mockups illustrate a fictional product and are not evidence of a functioning notebook application.
No condition mapping was inspected, no source artifact was edited and no numerical aesthetic score, universal winner or causal improvement claim is assigned.

processReview.summary: The baseline landing run executed its browser suite, revised readability and labels, then repeated verification and added targeted keyboard/HTML checks.

observations.observed: A public execution outline named visual construction, accessible controls, responsive layout and browser verification before the source write.
The candidate ran syntax validation and a browser verifier covering interactions, responsive states, no-JavaScript behavior and nested hosting.
After the initial suite passed, a command changed supporting text styles and illustration labels, then reran the same verifier successfully. No substantive test failure was recorded.
Additional inline checks exercised actual keyboard focus, mobile alternate panels and HTML/ARIA references. The README records executed checks and Chromium-only limits.

limits: No failed product test occurred in the trace, so recovery from a failure is not demonstrated here.
The self-authored verifier’s pass does not certify overall design or accessibility quality.
The native baseline already includes process guidance; this is not evidence of an instruction-free model.
This descriptive process audit was requested after outcomes existed. It is retrospective and exploratory, not a preregistered process endpoint.
The methods reviewer knows condition assignments; this review is not blinded. Separate proof/design reviewers have their own blinding procedures.
Only public progress messages, observable tool actions, check exits and retained artifact evidence are summarized. No hidden reasoning is inferred or published.
There is no process score, tool-call leaderboard or causal claim. More messages, calls, checks or elapsed time do not imply a better process.
The baseline retains native Codex instructions and the same common trial directions. It is not an unstructured or instruction-free model.
Delegation, external services and auxiliary model calls were prohibited for both conditions. Full orchestration, provider selection, collaboration and autonomous end-to-end deployment are unmeasured.
Treatment includes three or four pinned contracts plus a repository snapshot. Observed behavior cannot be assigned to an individual Fabius rule from this design.
Candidate-authored tests and self-reported passes are process evidence, not substitutes for the independent acceptance and proof checks.
Coverage includes all 12 finalized valid runs from the planned three-task, two-condition, two-repeat study. The two preserved setup attempts are documented separately.
